question: What is the role of extending rotational spectrum measurements of ethylene glycol to high frequencies in analyzing data from observatories like ALMA?
answer: Extending rotational spectrum measurements of ethylene glycol to high frequencies (up to 890 GHz) improves the accuracy of spectral line predictions, which is critical for analyzing data from observatories like ALMA. While lower-frequency extrapolations were sufficient for interpreting ALMA observations up to ~800 GHz, discrepancies arose in Band 10 (~800–950 GHz), necessitating direct high-frequency laboratory measurements. These refined spectra enable secure molecular detections in high-mass star-forming regions, such as NGC 6334I, and highlight the importance of high-frequency spectroscopic data for reliable astronomical interpretation.
